articles.title: New NFL Trade Rumors on Khalil Mack, Quentin Johnston, 'Inquiries' for Chargers' Vet Players
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Chargers reportedly aren't yet willing to sell off veteran players despite getting off to an 0-6 start this season.
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Chargers reportedly aren't yet willing to sell off veteran players despite getting off to an 0-6 start this season.

According to SI.com's Albert Breer , the Chargers have "shut down trade inquiries" thus far, as general manager Joe Hortiz and head coach Jim Harbaugh aren't yet looking to "wave any sort of white flag."

Pass-rusher Khalil Mack and wide receiver Quentin Johnston are two players Breer mentioned as having "questions" around them regarding their availability, but the Chargers reportedly aren't ready to start a fire sale yet.

L.A. is the last winless team remaining in the NFL this season, and unless the Chargers essentially run the table, it seems unlikely that the playoffs are in their immediate future.

The Bolts' schedule only appears to be getting tougher as well with a game against the Los Angeles Rams this weekend, followed by the Houston Texans and Baltimore Ravens the two weeks after that.

When the Chargers host the Texans on Nov. 8, the game will be played two days before the NFL trade deadline, and if Los Angeles loses one or even both of its next two games, perhaps the organization's stance will change.

It would be especially logical for the Chargers to move on from players set to hit free agency during the offseason, especially if they don't have designs on signing them to a new deal.

Mack, 35, signed a one-year deal to return to the Chargers this past offseason, and since he is nearing the end of his illustrious career, one would think he would like the chance to contend for a Super Bowl this season and perhaps even next season.

With three sacks through six games this season, Mack could provide a boost to a contender, and the Chargers would not only be doing him a favor by trading him, but they would be getting an asset back for a player they could lose for nothing in a few months anyway.

Trading a player like Johnston is less cut and dry since he is significantly younger than Mack and is signed through next season.

Originally selected 21st overall in the 2023 NFL draft by the Chargers, the 25-year-old Johnston has failed to live up to expectations.

He showed flashes last season and set a career high with 735 receiving yards, while also matching a career high with eight touchdowns, but he hasn't come close to that level this season.

Through five games, Johnston has registered just eight catches for 165 yards and no touchdowns.

Perhaps the Chargers would be willing to move Johnston if a team wants to take on his $16.4 million salary cap hit for next season, but it is fair to wonder if any team would want to do that given Johnston's lack of production this season.

articles.title: Greg Olsen Reportedly Seen as 'Favorite' to Replace Troy Aikman on 'Monday Night Football'
articles.summary: Amid the ongoing speculation about Troy Aikman's future in the Monday Night Football broadcast booth, ESPN is keeping an eye on Greg Olsen as a potential replacement candidate.
articles.body:
Amid the ongoing speculation about Troy Aikman's future in the Monday Night Football broadcast booth, ESPN is keeping an eye on Greg Olsen as a potential replacement candidate.

Per The Athletic's Andrew Marchand , Olsen is viewed as the "favorite" by people in the sports media industry to take over Aikman's role next to Joe Buck next season.

Sports media insider Richard Deitsch reported on Oct. 15 that Olsen's current contract with Fox is set to expire at the end of this season and the two sides have not had any discussions about a new deal thus far.

Aikman and Buck have been broadcast partners since 2002. They spent 20 seasons together at Fox before signing with ESPN in March 2022 to take over as the commentary crew for Monday Night Football.

This season marks the final year of the original contracts Aikman and Buck signed with ESPN. Buck got a new six-year deal from the network in September, leaving Aikman's status up in the air right now.

During an Oct. 16 appearance on 96.7 The Ticket in Dallas, Aikman said he is going to "free agent at the end of the year and kind of see what happens."

Olsen has been a full-time broadcaster as part of Fox Sports' NFL coverage since the 2021 season. He was part of the No. 1 team with play-by-play announcer Kevin Burkhardt and sideline reporters Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi during the 2022 season.

That group was on the call for Super Bowl 57 between the Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles.

After Tom Brady moved into broadcasting starting in 2023, Olsen has been paired with Joe Davis on the No. 2 team for Fox.

articles.title: Panthers Fire DC Ejiro Evero, Todd Wash Named Interim After Losses to Packers, Bucs
articles.summary: After allowing 70 points in two losses over the past four days, the Carolina Panthers are making a change at defensive coordinator.
articles.body:
After allowing 70 points in two losses over the past four days, the Carolina Panthers are making a change at defensive coordinator.

Panthers head coach Dave Canales announced on Friday that Ejiro Evero has been fired and defensive line coach Todd Wash will take over as defensive coordinator for the remainder of the season.

The Panthers also fired defensive pass game coordinator Jonathan Cooley.

Carolina followed up a 43-13 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Sunday with a 27-19 defeat against the Green Bay Packers on Thursday night.

The Panthers have allowed at least 26 points in four of their six games this season. Their season started by giving up 59 points and 552 yards to the Chicago Bears in Week 1. Both of those remain the highest single-game totals for any team in 2026.

Overall, the Panthers rank 27th in points allowed and 30th in rushing yards allowed per game. Their 12 rushing touchdowns allowed are the most by any defense.

Evero was in his fourth season as Carolina's defensive coordinator. He was hired in February 2023 by then-head coach Frank Reich and remained in his role after Canales took over in January 2024.

After finishing 29th and 32nd in points allowed during Evero's first two years as defensive coordinator, 2025 saw the unit take a step forward. The defense ranked 15th in points allowed, its highest ranking in that category since 2017.

Carolina was expected to take a step forward this season after making the playoffs last season. The offense has largely done its part with 25.4 points per game, ninth-best in the NFL.

But the struggles on defense are leading to the Panthers slowly falling down the NFC standings. Playing in the NFC South does help, as their 3-4 record has them tied with the Atlanta Falcons for first place.

Wash is also in his fourth season with the Panthers as a holdover from Reich's staff in 2023. He has five years of experience as a defensive coordinator from 2016 to '20 when he was with the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Carolina has a few extra days of rest before returning to play in Week 9 against the Denver Broncos at Bank of America Stadium.

articles.title: Jeffery Simmons Thanks Titans Fans After Blockbuster Trade to Bears, 'The Emotions Have Been High'
articles.summary: Star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons thanked the Tennessee Titans organization and Titans fans on Friday following his trade to the Chicago Bears this week.
articles.body:
Star defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons thanked the Tennessee Titans organization and Titans fans on Friday following his trade to the Chicago Bears this week.

In an Instagram post, Simmons wrote that "emotions have been high," adding that he "never thought" he would be writing a farewell message to the only home he has ever known at the NFL level:

The struggling Titans decided to part ways with Simmons on Thursday, sending him and a 2028 fifth-round pick to the Bears in exchange for first-round picks in 2027 and 2028, and a 2027 fourth-round pick.

Simmons' message, which saw him express his love and appreciation for the city of Nashville, came on the heels of the Titans paying tribute to him with an X post on Thursday night:

Originally selected 19th overall by the Titans in the 2019 NFL draft out of Mississippi State, Simmons established himself as one of the elite defensive tackles in the league during his eight-year tenure in Tennessee.

A four-time Pro Bowler and one-time First Team All-Pro, Simmons has recorded 46.5 sacks, 414 tackles and 72 tackles for loss in 106 career NFL regular-season games.

While Simmons never reached or won a Super Bowl with the Titans, he helped take them to the playoffs three times, including a trip to the AFC Championship Game in 2019.

Simmons has gotten better with age as well, setting new career highs in sacks (11), TFLs (17) and forced fumbles (three) last season.

He is also on a strong pace this season with 38 tackles and four sacks through seven games.

Despite Simmons' strong play, the Titans are just 1-6 this season, and they made the decision to part ways with their best player even though he is signed through 2030.

In Chicago, Simmons will have a chance to make the Bears legitimate Super Bowl contenders.

On the strength of head coach Ben Johnson's offense, the Bears fell just short of the NFC Championship Game last season, and after a 5-2 start, they look to be in the mix once again this season.

Simmons is the type of difference-maker Chicago's defense was missing, and with him now leading the defense and quarterback Caleb Williams leading the offense, the Bears will be a tough out come January.

articles.title: Travis Kelce vs Patrick Mahomes: Which Chiefs superstar has made a bigger impact through charitable donations and community work?
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have built extraordinary careers in Kansas City, winning championships and earning millions along the way.
articles.body: Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce have built extraordinary careers in Kansas City, winning championships and earning millions along the way. But their influence extends well beyond the football field. Both Chiefs superstars have invested heavily in charitable causes, supported children from disadvantaged backgrounds and helped strengthen their communities through their respective foundations. From Kelce's nearly $2 million contribution to Operation Breakthrough to Mahomes' multimillion-dollar grants for youth organisations, their generosity has become an important part of their legacies. While their approaches differ, their shared commitment raises an interesting question: Which Chiefs star has made a bigger impact through charity?Travis Kelce's charity work focuses on education and opportunities for underserved childrenKelce's charitable journey began with a personal connection to the struggles faced by young people. Growing up in Cleveland Heights, Ohio, the tight end saw how access to resources and opportunities could shape a child's future. That experience inspired him to establish the Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation in 2015.The organisation aims to help disadvantaged young people develop skills through education, business, athletics, science, technology, engineering, mathematics and the arts. Rather than limiting its work to financial assistance, Kelce's foundation focuses on giving children the tools to build independent futures.One of his most significant commitments has been his partnership with Operation Breakthrough, a Kansas City nonprofit that supports children and families experiencing poverty. Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to the organisation over the years through personal donations and directed funds, according to the Kansas City Chiefs.His most ambitious project with the organisation is the Ignition Lab. In 2020, Kelce announced plans to purchase an old building in Kansas City and transform it into a learning and workforce development centre for teenagers. The project became a reality in 2021, providing students aged 14 to 18 with opportunities to explore careers in engineering, automotive work, coding, digital media and entrepreneurship.The centre has helped more than 1,000 students since opening. Its purpose goes beyond classroom lessons, allowing teenagers to gain practical experience and discover possible career paths before entering adulthood.Kelce has also supported his hometown through the Heights Schools Foundation. His contributions have helped more than 2,300 children access remote learning, after-school programmes, tutoring and inspirational speakers.His generosity became particularly visible following the February 2024 Kansas City parade shooting. Two young sisters from the Reyes family suffered gunshot wounds during the incident. Kelce's Eighty-Seven & Running Foundation made two separate $50,000 donations to their family's fundraiser, bringing the total contribution to $100,000. The money helped cover their medical recovery and future needs.He has continued supporting Operation Breakthrough through annual fundraising events. His Celebrity Challenge brings together athletes from Kansas City's professional sports teams to raise money for the nonprofit. In October 2026, the event returned for its seventh edition.Kelce has also won Nationwide's Charity Challenge three times. His latest victory in January 2026 secured another $35,000 donation for Operation Breakthrough. He previously earned the same award in 2020 and 2025, making him the first three-time winner of the programme.Patrick Mahomes' foundation has distributed millions to children's charitiesWhile Kelce has built a strong connection with a few major organisations, Mahomes has developed a wider charitable network through his 15 and the Mahomies Foundation.Established in 2019, the foundation focuses on improving children's lives through health, education, wellness and community support. Patrick and his wife, Brittany Mahomes, have backed several projects across Kansas City and Texas, with grants reaching schools, youth organisations and community programmes.One of their biggest contributions came in 2021, when the foundation donated $1 million towards the redevelopment of Martin Luther King Jr. Park in Kansas City. The funding helped create an inclusive playground where children with different physical and mental abilities could play together.The project became an important community space, with accessible equipment and features designed to welcome children of all abilities. Mahomes also attended the opening ceremony, celebrating the playground with local families.In October 2023, the foundation announced another major commitment. It pledged $1.625 million to Boys & Girls Clubs of America through a multi-year partnership. The contribution supports children in Greater Kansas City, Lubbock, Tyler and Whitehouse, Texas.The partnership also introduced an additional fundraising element. The foundation committed to donating $1,500 for every regular-season touchdown scored by Mahomes, creating another way to connect his NFL performances with youth development.His foundation has also supported food security and children's healthcare. In 2022, it distributed more than 15,000 meals through food bank partnerships and worked with OneSight Vision Clinic to provide free eye examinations and glasses to more than 100 children in the Kansas City area.Mahomes has also supported the Make-A-Wish Foundation, granting wishes to 10 children with serious illnesses. His involvement included spending time with young fans and helping create memorable experiences for their families.Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce support different causes through their foundationsTheir charitable work shares a common goal, but the way they approach it reveals two different priorities.Kelce has built much of his philanthropic identity around long-term involvement. His relationship with Operation Breakthrough goes beyond writing cheques. He regularly visits the organisation, spends time with students and helps create programmes that can support children as they grow older.His foundation also supports educational opportunities in Cleveland Heights and Kansas City. The University of Cincinnati has benefited from his support through a health and wellness endowment for student-athletes.Mahomes, meanwhile, has developed a grant-based approach that reaches a wider network of organisations. His foundation has supported groups such as Lead to Read, City Year, United Way of Greater Kansas City, Children's Mercy Hospital, Special Olympics Missouri and Kansas City Public Library.The foundation's 2024 financial records provide an idea of its reach. According to nonprofit financial data, 15 and the Mahomies distributed approximately $4.6 million through 119 grants between 2020 and 2024. Its 2024 grants included $650,000 for Boys & Girls Clubs of America, $57,500 for City Year, $50,500 for Lead to Read and $50,000 for United Way of Greater Kansas City.Mahomes has also encouraged young people to become active in their communities through programmes such as Read for 15 and Volunteer for 15. These initiatives encourage children to spend time reading and helping others rather than focusing only on receiving financial assistance.The foundation has supported scholarship programmes, food assistance and inclusive sports opportunities as well. Its work with Special Olympics Missouri and other youth organisations reflects a broader effort to reach children with different needs.Who has made a bigger charitable impact, Travis Kelce or Patrick Mahomes?Comparing the two Chiefs stars through a single donation figure would miss much of the story. Their foundations operate differently, and their financial records cover different periods.Kelce has contributed nearly $2 million to Operation Breakthrough alone, while his work with Ignition Lab has created lasting educational and career opportunities for teenagers. His $100,000 contribution to the Reyes family and repeated fundraising victories also demonstrate his willingness to support families facing difficult circumstances.Mahomes has a wider documented grant portfolio. His foundation distributed approximately $4.6 million across 119 grants between 2020 and 2024, alongside major commitments such as the $1 million playground project and the $1.625 million Boys & Girls Clubs partnership.However, the foundation's grant totals should not be treated as Mahomes' personal donations. They include money raised and distributed through the charitable organisation and its partners. The same distinction applies to Kelce's foundation contributions.What stands out is how both players have turned their success into opportunities for others. Kelce has developed a close connection with young people through education and career development, while Mahomes has used his foundation to support a wider range of organisations.Their approaches may be different, but their impact reaches beyond football. For Kansas City, having two of its biggest sporting stars invest in the next generation could prove just as meaningful as the trophies they have won.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Chiefs’ Justin Tucker decision triggers media clash as Emmanuel Acho turns Mina Kimes and Nick Wright’s criticism against them
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign Justin Tucker has sparked a debate that goes beyond the veteran kicker’s ability on the field.
articles.body: The Kansas City Chiefs’ decision to sign Justin Tucker has sparked a debate that goes beyond the veteran kicker’s ability on the field. ESPN analysts Mina Kimes and Nick Wright questioned the move, raising concerns about the risks of bringing Tucker into Kansas City. Emmanuel Acho, however, challenged their criticism, turning the discussion toward the standards used to judge the Chiefs’ decision. The disagreement highlights a difficult question for the team: how much risk should a contender accept when looking for answers at a position where one missed kick can change a game?Emmanuel Acho challenges Mina Kimes and Nick Wright over their Justin Tucker criticismAcho’s response focused less on Tucker’s kicking record and more on what he sees as inconsistent standards across the NFL. The former linebacker argued that critics cannot single out one player while continuing to support a league where other players have faced serious allegations or been involved in troubling incidents.“If you want to call out Justin Tucker, which I have no issue with you doing, you’ve got to call out everybody on every team, including coaches,” Acho said.His argument was direct. Acho acknowledged the seriousness of the allegations against Tucker but questioned why the backlash appeared focused on one case. He also challenged Kimes and Wright to consider their roles as analysts who continue to cover and celebrate the sport.The controversy is not based on a settled finding of wrongdoing. In 2025, The Baltimore Banner reported that 16 massage therapists accused Tucker of sexual misconduct. The allegations concerned incidents at eight Baltimore-area spas and wellness centers between 2012 and 2016. Tucker has denied the accusations, calling them “unequivocally false.”Kimes drew attention to the allegations after the Chiefs announced the signing, sharing a screenshot of the report on social media. Wright was more explicit about his opposition, writing, “Going on the record that I hope Justin Tucker never plays a snap for the Chiefs.”Acho challenged both commentators over the difference between condemning a player and continuing to support the wider league. His criticism raises a genuine question about where sports media figures should draw the line, although opposing a signing does not automatically require someone to stop covering the NFL.Chiefs’ kicking problems add another layer to the debateKansas City’s decision also has a clear football explanation. Harrison Butker has struggled this season, missing five of his 16 field-goal attempts. His latest difficulties came in the Chiefs’ 20-3 loss to the Seattle Seahawks, when he missed two kicks and Kansas City managed only three points.Tucker, a five-time All-Pro, offers a chance to assess an experienced kicker who was once among the NFL’s most reliable. However, he has not played in an NFL game since 2024. He also missed the entire 2025 season after receiving a 10-game suspension for violating the league’s personal conduct policy.Chiefs coach Andy Reid offered little detail when asked about the decision, saying, “He’s done his suspension. Took care of his business there. I’ll leave it at that.”For now, Tucker is on the practice squad, while Butker remains Kansas City’s kicker on the active roster. The signing does not guarantee Tucker will play, and the Chiefs still have to decide whether his potential on the field outweighs the questions surrounding his return.That distinction matters. Kansas City can evaluate Tucker as a possible solution to its kicking problems, but the move also brings scrutiny that cannot be settled by statistics alone. Acho has shifted the debate toward the consistency of the media’s response, while Kimes and Wright have made their objections clear. articles.summary: The Chicago Bears revealed that four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who officially arrived in town via trade on Thursday, will wear No. 99.
articles.body:
The Chicago Bears revealed that four-time Pro Bowl defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons, who officially arrived in town via trade on Thursday, will wear No. 99.

The Bears acquired Simmons and a 2028 fifth-round draft pick from the Titans for 2027 and 2028 first-round selections and a 2027 fourth-round choice.

Simmons wore No. 98 for seven-plus seasons with Tennessee. However, Bears defensive end Montez Sweat—who was college teammates with Simmons at Mississippi State—has No. 98.

The former Bulldogs star had his best NFL season in 2025, amassing a career-high 11 sacks, 67 tackles (39 solo) and 21 quarterback hits. He earned All-Pro First Team honors.

Simmons has continued his standout play in 2026, racking up four sacks, 38 tackles (20 solo) and nine quarterback hits in seven games.

Now the 5-2 Bears have him aboard just in time for a huge NFC battle on Monday evening at the defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks. Kickoff is set for 8:15 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Colts' Josh Downs to Play vs. Jaguars Despite Reported Trade Request Ahead of NFL Deadline
articles.summary: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs will play Sunday at the Jacksonville Jaguars despite his trade request, head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Friday.
articles.body:
Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Josh Downs will play Sunday at the Jacksonville Jaguars despite his trade request , head coach Shane Steichen told reporters on Friday.

The 2-5 Colts have already traded left guard Quenton Nelson to the Seattle Seahawks and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to the San Francisco 49ers amid a disappointing year that has included the firing of general manager Chris Ballard on Oct. 19.

Downs is in his fourth NFL season and the final year of his rookie contract. The former UNC star, who was a third-round pick in the 2023 draft, has caught 26 passes for 307 yards in seven games this year.

One can safely assume his time with the Colts is arriving at its end, whether it's via a trade before the Nov. 10 deadline or in free agency next offseason.

It's possible the end could happen sooner rather than later.

Teams are certainly in need of wide receiver help. Of note, NFL insider James Palmer reported on Prime on Thursday night that the Kansas City Chiefs and Pittsburgh Steelers are both looking for wideouts.

The Colts have already made it clear that they are conducting a fire sale as they presumably enter a rebuild, so trading Downs before he can leave for nothing in free agency makes sense.

In the meantime, Indianapolis is forging ahead amid a tough season that's seen the team lose three straight. A hard matchup at the 4-2 and first-place Jaguars now looms. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET on Sunday.

articles.title: Lamar Jackson's Status for Ravens vs. Bills Revealed by Jesse Minter amid Ankle Injury
articles.summary: Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday he'll be back on the field Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.
articles.body:
Lamar Jackson has missed the last three games with an ankle injury, but Baltimore Ravens head coach Jesse Minter confirmed Friday he'll be back on the field Sunday against the Buffalo Bills.

Jackson told reporters he's feeling "better" after being diagnosed with a high ankle sprain.

Jackson's exact status has been something of a question mark, as he practiced some before Baltimore's game against the Cincinnati Bengals but didn't take the field.

Minter was asked about the overall messaging surrounding the injury since he previously called Jackson "day-to-day" while the quarterback said it was a high ankle sprain that prevented him from running.

"When the player is healthy enough to play, they'll play," Minter said while also reiterating the team will know more Wednesday. "… There's things that change sometimes with injuries and what you think of it right when it happens in a game where the adrenaline and things are still going on."

Tyler Huntley has played for Jackson during the starter's absence and led the team to a victory over the Atlanta Falcons before losing to the Cleveland Browns and Bengals in AFC North games.

Baltimore is now 4-3 overall but 0-2 in the division and in last place.

The Ravens will look to get back in the win column Sunday when Jackson is back under center to face Josh Allen and the Bills.

articles.title: Packers RB Josh Jacobs says hands-behind-back gesture after first-half TD vs. Panthers was ode to gospel song
articles.summary: Jacobs was arrested in May and ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property.
articles.body:
Green Bay Packers running back Josh Jacobs told reporters postgame Thursday night that his first-half touchdown celebration was an ode to the gospel song "Break Every Chain."

After scoring from 1 yard out in the second quarter of a 27-19 win over the Carolina Panthers at Lambeau Field , the Prime Video broadcast showed a glimpse of the controversial celebration , which began with him putting his hands behind his back.

That clip instantly circulated online, with many interpreting that gesture as Jacobs mocking his May arrest, for which he ultimately pleaded no contest to misdemeanor charges of battery and criminal damage to property .

Jacobs was clearly bothered by that connection and denied it.

"They didn't even get the whole celebration," Jacobs said, via ESPN's Rob Demovsky , noting, "It was f***ing one second that they just showed me."

Jacobs explained that he and Packers wide receiver Savion Williams came up with the celebration.

"Basically, last week, we said the first celebration, when I score, I was going to thank God — that's what I did last week," Jacobs said. "The second one was going to be 'Break Every Chain.' It's a gospel song. That was going to be the next celebration. It's just a correlation, but, like I said, the media [is] going to run with it. They're going to make it something that it wasn't, but it is what it is."

Not long after the 28-year-old Jacobs hopped into the end zone to give the Packers a 13-10 lead, he put his hands behind his back and walked forward a couple steps. Later, Jacobs and Williams can be seen completing the celebration together.

"I didn't think it was going to be a thing that can be perceived a certain type of way," Jacobs said, per ESPN . "But it's 2026, and it is what it is."

Jacobs finished the night with 39 rushing yards on 21 carries, averaging a mere 1.9 yards per tote. He did score that TD, though, along with another one in third quarter on a 4-yard reception. The three-time Pro Bowl back caught six passes for 13 yards in the victory.

He landed on that list in the aftermath of his spring altercation with a woman at his Green Bay area home .

Back in September, Jacobs was reportedly convicted of battery and fined $1,000. Additionally, per ESPN , he accepted a deferred judgment agreement on the criminal damage to property charge.

Jacobs was reportedly ordered to pay restitution, attend counseling, avoid contact with the victim and be supervised for one year.

Upon being removed from the commissioner exempt list earlier this month, Jacobs said he was "remorseful" and "sorry for putting this team in this situation."

At the time, he added, among other things: "Going forward just trying to be better. I know for some people this might be a stain on me and my character. I feel like I don't have to really speak on my character. A lotta people that know me in this locker room, or that's been around me, I'll let them do that."

The NFL's investigation into Jacobs' potential violations of the personal conduct policy is ongoing. Once that investigation wraps, Jacobs could receive a suspension from the league. That said, time served on the commissioner exempt list can count toward a suspension.

articles.title: New NFL Rumors on Mike Tomlin's Potential Return, 'High Demand' Ahead of Coaching Carousel
articles.summary: Football Night in America analyst and ex-Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin would reportedly be in "extremely high demand" if he left the broadcast booth back for the sidelines, but "it's not considered automatic" that he'd make the return, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.
articles.body:
Football Night in America analyst and ex-Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike Tomlin would reportedly be in "extremely high demand" if he left the broadcast booth back for the sidelines, but "it's not considered automatic" that he'd make the return, per Mark Maske of Front Office Sports.

"Mike Tomlin is expected to be in extremely high demand as an NFL head coaching candidate in the coming months, but it's not considered automatic that he would leave his broadcasting job at NBC to accept a big-money coaching offer, sources tell Front Office Sports.

"It's believed that Tomlin's contract with NBC would allow him to depart the network for an NFL coaching job. But other factors, such as the demands of coaching as compared to those in his promising broadcasting career, are expected to receive consideration, according to those sources."

Report: Olsen 'Favorite' to Replace Aikman

Tomlin, 54, spent 19 seasons (2007-2025) as the Steelers' head coach, going 193-114-2, making 13 playoff appearances and winning eight AFC North titles, two AFC Championships and one Super Bowl.

After the 2025 season, Tomlin stepped down as head coach. He now has a great gig with NBC, which he seems to be enjoying quite well.

So no one can blame Tomlin if he decides the broadcasting life is for him in the present and future.

However, if Tomlin wants to get back into coaching, it's no surprise teams would be calling given his tremendous resume and lengthy history of success.

None of Tomlin's teams ever finished with a record under .500, and making the playoffs more often than not over two decades is a remarkable feat.

Head coaching positions always open up in the NFL. In fact, there have been at least five head coaching changes in each of the last 16 seasons, including 10 coaching changes last offseason, per ESPN .

Tomlin should therefore have his chance to head back to the NFL if he wants. The question is whether that'll be the case.

articles.title: Cowboys' Jerry Jones Reveals Stipulation Required to Make Trade at 2026 NFL Deadline
articles.summary: In the aftermath of three NFC playoff contenders making significant trades to improve their rosters this week, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't necessarily feeling pressure to respond with a deal of his own.
articles.body:
In the aftermath of three NFC playoff contenders making significant trades to improve their rosters this week, Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones isn't necessarily feeling pressure to respond with a deal of his own.

Appearing on Friday's episode of The K&C Masterpiece on 105.3 The Fan (h/t The Athletic's Jon Machota ), Jones said the Cowboys would need to find a "dynamic situation to give up picks" in a trade.

Insider: 'All Hell' to Break Loose at Deadline

The NFC landscape was altered dramatically this week. It started on Tuesday when the Seattle Seahawks added Quenton Nelson in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts, followed a few hours later by the San Francisco 49ers acquiring DeForest Buckner.

Things hit another level on Thursday when the Chicago Bears traded two first-round picks to the Chicago Bears in a package All-Pro defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons.

Dallas is in a bit of an awkward position with less than two weeks remaining before the trade deadline. The Cowboys sit at 3-4 through seven games, two games behind the New York Giants in the loss column for first place in the NFC East.

Their issues from last season have carried over into 2026, with the defense frequently holding back one of the league's best offenses. They rank 23rd in points allowed, 27th in defensive success rate and 30th in EPA allowed per play.

Another issue, along with their current spot in the standings, is how much the Cowboys have invested over the past 12 months in trying to figure out their defense.

Jones sent a 2028 second-round pick to the Pittsburgh Steelers for Joey Porter Jr. on Oct. 1. Prior to last year's trade deadline, he gave up a 2027 first-round pick to the New York Jets for Quinnen Williams.

Josh Sweat of the Arizona Cardinals has started to pop up as a potential trade target for the Cowboys, but it could depend on the cost if Dallas can make it happen.

The Cowboys currently only have four picks in the upcoming draft. Hypothetically, if they were to send a 2027 second-rounder to Arizona, all of their own picks would be gone. Their selections would be coming from the Green Bay Packers (first round), Pittsburgh Steelers (fourth round) and New England Patriots (seventh round).

articles.title: Appeals court reverses rejection of damages award against NFL in Sunday Ticket class action
articles.summary: NFL undoubtedly will appeal the ruling to the U.S. Supreme Court.
articles.body:
This is the kind of Friday afternoon bad news dump that counts as horrible news for the NFL.

Via Mike Scarcella of Reuters, the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Ninth Circuit has reinstated the $4.7 billion verdict in the Sunday Ticket class action.

The Reuters article, however, apparently has misread the decision. Mark Maske of Front Office Sports characterizes the outcome as ordering a new trial on damages .

"The jury clearly awarded damages based on its improper consideration of the evidence rather than according to the district court's instructions," the Ninth Circuit wrote. "This warrants a new trial on damages. We remand this case for the district court to reinstate the jury's liability verdict and hold a new damages trial."

A new trial on damages could result in a lower (or similar or, in theory, higher) final verdict.

The original award, given by a jury in July 2024, was scrapped by the presiding judge over concerns regarding the evidence the plaintiffs presented of economic harm. The judge did not throw out the finding that the NFL had violated federal antitrust laws in the pricing of the Sunday Ticket package.

If/when any verdict becomes an official judgment, the damages will be tripled.

The original verdict sent shock waves through the league, since it ultimately would require each team to come up with $440 million in cash. Statutory interest will push that number even higher.

The NFL undoubtedly will appeal the final decision to the U.S. Supreme Court, which would first have to decide whether to accept the case before issuing a decision. The case possibly would not be ripe for an appeal to the Supreme Court until a new trial on damages happens — if that's what the Ninth Circuit has indeed ordered.

Whatever happens next, the situation instantly becomes the most consequential piece of litigation in the 100-plus-year history of the league.

That says a lot. Grab the Bengals as a streamer, and consider keeping them for a while.

How brave can you be? The Cowboys rank No. 29 in the NFL in yards allowed. They are dead last against the run, giving up 145,7 yards per game. And they are No. 25 in points allowed.

Furthermore, they are No. 30 in the league with only four takeaways all season. Plus, the Cardinals have turned the ball over only six times all year, with six interceptions and zero fumbles lost.

"Plus, this Cowboys unit has multiple sacks and an interception in back-to-back games. So, I'll take it versus a Cardinals offense ranking in the bottom 10 in both scoring and yards per game."

Another thing to consider is Jacoby Brissett. He's on pace for a career high in interceptions, as he has already chucked six to the opponents this season in 282 passing attempts. It wouldn't be surprising to see the Cowboys get their mitts on a pair of picks in this matchup.

Plus, the Cowboys defense has talent. It absolutely does. Using them as a streaming defense is betting on the talent.

Big plays are on the board for this matchup. If the Cowboys can cash one of them in, they will have lived up to their streaming value.

"Among 40 qualifying passers, he is bottom of the barrel, ranking 39th in yards per attempt, passing success rate, and catchable target rate," Fitzmaurice wrote. "McKee couldn't take advantage of a struggling Dallas secondary last week, so I have zero faith that he'll be able to do much against Washington this week."

The Commanders' defense could have their best game of the season this week. And maybe it's their last good game of the season because they've already played the Eagles once.

Plus, the Commanders are coming off a good second half against the 49ers, according to The Washington Post.

"Washington pressured quarterback Brock Purdy on 50 percent of his dropbacks Oct. 19 in Santa Clara, California — the team's highest rate in any half this season, according to the analytics platform TruMedia," Tashan Reed wrote. Nice. And how much better are the 49ers than the Eagles? Light years. There's a real possibility of a good effort from the Commanders' defense this week.
